Real-time Event Clock forecast

Source: R/measure.R
event_clock_forecast.Rd

Before an option expires we do not yet know how much information will arrive while it is alive. A real-time forecast uses only prices observed up to the valuation time at: it measures the recent speed of the clock (log-odds variation per calendar day over an estimation window) and multiplies it by the remaining horizon, $$\widehat A^{rt}(h) = \frac{\widehat A(\text{window})} {\text{window length in days}} \times h.$$

Usage

event_clock_forecast(
  x,
  at = NULL,
  horizon,
  trailing = ec_default_params()$trailing,
  days = NULL,
  expanding = FALSE,
  method = "rv",
  interval = NULL,
  sample_every = ec_default_params()$sample_every,
  trunc_sd = ec_default_params()$trunc_sd,
  scale_fn = stats::mad,
  clip = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An event_prices object (see as_event_prices()), or a data.frame coercible to one.

at

Valuation date/time at which the forecast is made (default: last observation). Only observations at or before at are used.

horizon

Forecast horizon(s): either numeric (days) or Date/POSIXct horizon dates (converted to days from at; POSIXct horizons give fractional days). Names are used as labels.

trailing

Integer, number of trailing observations in the estimation window (default 40). Ignored when days or expanding is set.

days

Numeric, length of a trailing calendar-day window.

expanding

Logical; use all observations up to at.

method

Estimator for the window (default "rv"; see event_clock()).

interval

Optional sampling interval in minutes for staggered grid sampling of intraday data.

sample_every

Integer, use every k-th observation (sparse-sampling robustness; default 1).

trunc_sd

Numeric, truncation threshold in robust standard deviations (default 3).

scale_fn

Function computing the robust scale of the increments for truncated (default stats::mad()).

clip

Numeric length-2 clipping bounds for q before the log-odds transform; defaults to the bounds stored in x.

Value

A tibble with columns market_id, at, horizon, horizon_days, rule (window and estimator), trailing (window size for observation windows, else NA), method, n_incr, n_gaps, max_gap_days, rate_per_day, and A_forecast. See event_clock() for the gap diagnostics.

Details

Three kinds of estimation window are available. By default the window is the last trailing observations and its length is their calendar span. With days, the window is the last days calendar days before at (e.g. days = 3 with hourly data); with expanding = TRUE it is the whole history up to at. Any estimator of event_clock() can measure the window (method), and with intraday data interval turns on staggered grid sampling as in event_clock_staggered().

Which window works best is an empirical question. Choose it the way the accompanying working paper does — by forecast accuracy on earlier option lives only, never on the options being tested — with ec_forecast_select().

See also

ec_forecast_select() to choose the window by forecast accuracy; ec_recovery_set() for the low-clock sensitivity.

Examples

data(us2016)
ep <- as_event_prices(us2016, time = "date", price = "trump")
# trailing 60 increments, as selected for this series in the paper
event_clock_forecast(ep, at = as.Date("2016-10-10"),
                     horizon = c(`1W` = 7, `2W` = 14), trailing = 61)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 12
#>   market_id at         horizon horizon_days rule   trailing method n_incr n_gaps
#>   <chr>     <date>     <chr>          <dbl> <chr>     <int> <chr>   <int>  <int>
#> 1 NA        2016-10-10 1W                 7 trail…       61 rv         60      0
#> 2 NA        2016-10-10 2W                14 trail…       61 rv         60      0
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: max_gap_days <dbl>, rate_per_day <dbl>, A_forecast <dbl>

# hourly data: clock speed over the last three days
data(polymarket2024)
event_clock_forecast(as_event_prices(polymarket2024),
  at = as.POSIXct("2024-10-25 19:45", tz = "UTC"),
  horizon = as.POSIXct("2024-11-01 19:45", tz = "UTC"), days = 3)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 12
#>   market_id at                  horizon       horizon_days rule  trailing method
#>   <chr>     <dttm>              <chr>                <dbl> <chr>    <int> <chr> 
#> 1 NA        2024-10-25 19:45:00 2024-11-01 1…            7 trai…       NA rv    
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_incr <int>, n_gaps <int>, max_gap_days <dbl>,
#> #   rate_per_day <dbl>, A_forecast <dbl>
